newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX crawls to lower close, dollar weighs.
newsitem.headline: German DAX crawls to lower close, dollar weighs.

text.p: Germany's blue-chip DAX index ended bourse trade lower on Friday following an overnight decline on Wall Street and some pressure on the dollar, but dealers said the decline did not mark a clear trend.
Cash market orders were thin with activity dominated by options dealers due to an expiry deadline for options on the DAX index and some constituents.
The 30-share DAX closed down 38.86 points, or 1.15 percent, at 3,344.39 points, with export-driven car and chemical shares suffering the largest losses.
The bulk of the decline was a catch-up with losses that occured in post-bourse trade on Thursday after comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer against a weak mark undermined the dollar.

The DAX remained in a nine-point range for the whole session on Friday. "Things are often quiet like this when we have a small options expiry," said a Frankfurt trader. "I wouldn't overplay this move at the moment."
There were few outstanding movements among blue chip shares. Chemical giant Hoechst AG fell sharply, down 2.10 marks or 3.2 percent, at 64.35 marks.
Dealers linked Hoechst's decline with presentations the company had made to investors in London, while the lower dollar also contributed to the fall.
Other chemical stocks to take a fall included BASF AG, which was down 1.10 marks, or 1.6 percent, at 66.40.
Daimler-Benz AG, another decliner from Thursday, was also under pressure, down 1.80 marks, or 1.4 percent, at 131.50.
BMW AG and Porsche AG, two darlings of the stock market in recent weeks, were both sharply lower as sentiment in car shares was hit by the lower dollar.
BMW fell 48.50 marks, or 3.4 percent, to 1,382.50 marks, while Porsche was down 70 marks, or 3.3 percent, at 2,060 marks.
